big_ideas.title: The stance is the root
big_ideas.text: Every technique is built on a standard base — foot angles, thigh height, weight split, alignment of knee over foot. Judges deduct, and stunts fail, at the base first.

big_ideas.title: Power is whole-body and sequenced
big_ideas.text: Force comes from the floor, through legs and waist, out through the hands or weapon; hands, eyes, body and steps arrive together. Isolated limbs look weak on the carpet and on camera.

big_ideas.title: Each style is a coherent set of principles
big_ideas.text: Changquan (extension, speed, height), nanquan (rooted stances, bridge arms, short explosive power, sound) and taijiquan (continuity, softness, rising-sinking control) each answer "what is good movement" differently; weapons extend the same body method.

big_ideas.title: Jumps and spins obey mechanics
big_ideas.text: Takeoff impulse fixes flight time; angular momentum is made on the floor and conserved in the air; shape changes trade inertia for spin; landings are impulse problems. Most faults are a mechanical cause, not a mystery.

big_ideas.title: The score is an explicit model of quality
big_ideas.text: Quality of movement (deduction codes), overall performance (graded bands) and degree of difficulty (coded elements and connections) make "good wushu" concrete and checkable.

big_ideas.title: Performance communicates
big_ideas.text: Rhythm, spirit (jingshen) and eyes (yanshen) turn correct technique into a performance; for screen work the same principles serve the camera, under strict partner safety.

practices.title: Name and classify
practices.text: Give a technique its Chinese (pinyin + characters) and English names, its family (stance, hand form, step, kick, balance, jump, tumbling, weapon method) and its code.

practices.title: Observe and diagnose
practices.text: Compare a described or filmed execution to the standard and locate the fault precisely (which joint, which angle, which phase).

practices.title: Apply the rules
practices.text: Assign deduction codes and values, difficulty and connection values, apply caps and judge-panel rules, and compute a score.

practices.title: Explain the mechanism
practices.text: Give the biomechanical or stylistic reason a technique works or fails, and the change that fixes it.

practices.title: Perform and self-assess
practices.text: Execute to standard, film it, check it against the criteria, and log the result.

practices.title: Compose and adapt
practices.text: Build or edit a routine or fight phrase to a constraint — rules, music, carpet, camera, partner.

los.do: Identify a changquan stance from its description and give its pinyin, characters and English name (drillable both directions).
ek: Gongbu 弓步 bow · mabu 马步 horse · xubu 虚步 empty · pubu 仆步 drop · xiebu 歇步 cross-legged crouch · zuopan 坐盘 cross-legged sitting.

los.do: State the standard alignment of gongbu and mabu and name the deduction criteria that test it.
ek: Gongbu: front knee over instep, front thigh level, rear leg straight, rear sole flat, rear foot turned in (code 50).
Mabu: feet wider than shoulders and parallel, thighs level, knees not caving, heels down, toes not out ≥ 45° (code 51).

los.do: State the standard alignment of xubu, pubu and xiebu and identify which standard a described stance breaks.
ek: Xubu: weight on the rear leg, rear thigh level, rear heel down (52).
Pubu: squatting thigh on calf, extended leg straight, extended foot turned in and flat (53).
Xiebu: legs crossed, buttock resting on the rear calf (54).

los.do: Hold each standard stance for time and film it front and side, checking every criterion.
ek: Stance holds (zhan zhuang) build the leg endurance that keeps thighs level late in a routine.

los.do: Identify a hand form from its description and name it in Chinese and English, including the nanquan forms.
ek: Quan 拳 fist · zhang 掌 palm · gou 勾 hook · jianzhi 剑指 sword fingers; nanquan adds hu zhao 虎爪 tiger claw, he zui 鹤嘴 crane's beak, single-finger palm.

los.do: Assign the code for a described hand-form fault.
ek: 01 fist face uneven or thumb not on the middle finger · 02 palm fingers apart or thumb not tucked · 03 hook fingers not pinched or wrist not fully hooked · 04 sword fingers not straight and together. 0.1 each.

los.do: Identify a step from its description and name it in Chinese and English.
ek: Shangbu 上步 step up · tuibu 退步 step back · gaibu 盖步 cover step (in front) · chabu 插步 insert step (behind) · jibu 击步 strike-hop · genbu 跟步 follow-up step · qilinbu 麒麟步 unicorn step (nanquan).

los.do: Explain why the centre of gravity should not bob during stepping, and assign the taiji step fault code.
ek: Level CoM keeps the next technique available and reads as control; taiji code 59: knee–toe misaligned, foot dragged, CoM rises/falls, foot raised too high.

topics.title: Flexibility and basic leg techniques (tui fa 腿法)

los.do: Identify a basic kick from its description (path, contact surface, straight or bent) and name it in Chinese and English.
ek: Straight-leg swings: zhengtitui 正踢腿 front stretch, waibaitui 外摆腿 outside crescent, lihetui 里合腿 inside crescent. Bent-straight: tantui 弹腿 snap, dengtui 蹬腿 heel push, chuaitui 踹腿 side kick. Slaps: paijiao 拍脚. Sweeps: qiansaotui 前扫腿, housaotui 后扫腿.

los.do: Assign the code for a described kick or sweep fault.
ek: 20 front sweep: supporting thigh above level, sweeping sole lifts, sweeping leg bent ≥ 45° · 21 back sweep · 23 snap/heel/side kick not fully straightened · 24 stretch kick: knee bent at apex or supporting heel up · 25 slap kick: toes below shoulder or slap missed.

los.do: Contrast a TKD kick with its nearest wushu counterpart and name the habit that will cost a deduction.
ek: TKD chambers and strikes with the ball/instep; wushu straight-leg kicks swing from the hip with a locked knee and slap the foot. A chambered 'stretch kick' bends at the apex (code 24); a TKD 'tornado' is a spinning roundhouse, a wushu xuanfengjiao is an inside-crescent slap.

los.do: Plan a flexibility block (dynamic before, static after) that targets the ranges that limit front split, pubu and slap height.
ek: Hamstrings and hip flexors gate split and stretch-kick height; adductors and ankle dorsiflexion gate pubu. Dynamic swings warm up; long static holds belong after training.

los.do: Explain changquan's defining qualities and how each shows in a stance, a kick and a jump.
ek: Long extension, speed, height and clear stops; derived from chaquan, huaquan, hongquan and Shaolin. Extended limbs, high kicks, big jumps, sharp dong–jing (motion–stillness) contrast.

los.do: Match each of the twelve changquan 'shapes' (十二型) to the quality it demands.
ek: 动如涛 move like waves · 静如岳 still like a mountain · 起如猿 rise like an ape · 落如鹊 land like a magpie · 立如鸡 stand like a rooster · 站如松 stand like a pine · 转如轮 turn like a wheel · 折如弓 bend like a bow · 轻如叶 light as a leaf · 重如铁 heavy as iron · 缓如鹰 slow like a hawk · 快如风 fast as wind.

los.do: Name the hand and leg methods in a described changquan combination and state the stance each must finish in.
ek: Chongquan 冲拳 punch, tuizhang 推掌 push palm, liangzhang 亮掌 flash palm; each strike arrives with the stance, not after it.

los.do: Perform a basic changquan combination to standard, filmed, and self-score it against the stance and hand-form codes.
ek: Self-scoring with the A-codes is the cheapest feedback loop: one code per fault per occurrence.

los.do: Identify which standard routine set a described changquan routine belongs to and what it is used for (compulsory event, junior Group B, Duanwei exam).
ek: The 1989 CWA-approved international set covers changquan, nanquan, taijiquan, daoshu, jianshu, gunshu, qiangshu; compulsory routines remove choreography choice so judges compare like with like.

los.do: Learn a compulsory changquan routine section by section and log which movements fall under which deduction codes.
ek: Mapping each movement to its codes turns a routine into a checklist of judgeable standards.

los.do: Explain how nanquan differs from changquan in stance height, power and acrobatics.
ek: From Hung Ga, Choy Li Fut and similar: fewer acrobatics and less flexibility demand, more leg stability and short explosive power from legs–hips–shoulders; vocal fa sheng 发声 is part of the style.

los.do: Identify a nanquan stance from its description, name it, and state how its thigh standard differs from changquan.
ek: Diebu 蝶步 butterfly stance, guibu 跪步 kneeling, qilongbu 骑龙步 dragon-riding join gongbu, mabu, xubu, pubu. Nanquan thighs sit 0–45° above level (codes 50–52, 57), not flat as in changquan.

los.do: Assign the code for a described nanquan stance fault.
ek: 55 diebu: inner calf or heel of the kneeling leg off the carpet · 56 kneeling: knee on carpet or buttock off calf · 57 dragon-riding: rear knee on carpet or front thigh out of range.

los.do: List the mandatory nanquan techniques an optional routine must contain and identify a missing one in a described routine.
ek: Tiger claw; guagai quan 挂盖拳 and pao quan 抛拳; gun qiao 滚桥 rolling bridge; six stances (gong, ma, pu, xu, die, qilong); qilinbu; heng ding tui 横钉腿 horizontal nail kick. Missing a mandatory technique is a code-80 deduction.

los.do: Explain what bridge arms (qiao 桥) do and why short power (duan jin) needs a rooted stance.
ek: The forearm bridge controls the opponent's arm at close range; with little travel, force must come from ground reaction through a fixed base — a rising stance bleeds it.

los.do: Explain the body-method requirements of taijiquan and assign the posture code for a described fault.
ek: Head upright, shoulders sunk, elbows down, armpits open, back not rounded, buttocks not out; code 05 hand technique (elbow lifted, arm locked, armpit closed), 06 posture (shrugged, rounded, twisted, protruding).

los.do: Identify which taiji source styles a competition routine draws on and what that means for its look.
ek: Competition taiji is largely Yang-style with Chen, Wu, Wu (Hao) and Sun elements; it adds balances and jumps and is performed to music.

los.do: Explain why taiji demands continuity and a level centre of gravity, and how a judge would see a break.
ek: Taiji power is continuous transfer; a pause before a difficulty element (code 83) or a bob in the CoM (59) shows the movement was not connected.

los.do: Match a standard taiji routine to its name and competition time limit.
ek: 24-form simplified and 42-form taijijian: 4–5 min; 42-form taijiquan and style routines: 5–6 min; 32-form taijijian: 3–4 min (iwuf-2024).

los.do: Perform the 24-form with continuous tempo, filmed, and check stance and step codes 50–53 and 59.
ek: Taiji stance standards differ: bow-stance rear knee may not collapse inward; empty-stance front heel may not touch.

los.do: Identify a sword or broadsword method from its description and name it in Chinese and English.
ek: Jian 剑: ci 刺 thrust, pi 劈 chop, liao 撩 upward cut, dian 点 point, beng 崩 snap, gua 挂 hook-parry, chou/dai 抽带 draw. Dao 刀: chantou 缠头 and guonao 裹脑 wrap around head, pi, kan 砍, hua 花 flower.

los.do: Explain the stylistic contrast between jian and dao.
ek: '刀如猛虎，剑如飞凤' — broadsword fierce like a tiger, straight sword graceful like a flying phoenix: dao drives with the body, jian is light with precise tip work.

los.do: Assign the code for a described jian or dao fault.
ek: 60 hook-parry/uppercut without a clear vertical circle · 61 finger touching the blade on the guard · 62 dao back not close to the body in chantou/guonao · 68 jian envelopment tip not tracing a circle.

los.do: Identify a staff or spear method from its description and name it.
ek: Qiang 枪: lan 拦, na 拿, zha 扎 (block, seize, thrust); gun 棍: pi, beng, pao, horizontal and vertical wuhua 舞花 (figure-8).

los.do: Assign the code for a described gun or qiang fault.
ek: 63 spear: head not in a defined arc, tail protruding past the rear hand, thrust not level · 64 horizontal windmill without a clear circle · 65 vertical figure-8 not in a vertical plane · 67 nangun plant: end not planted or tip below head.

los.do: Explain why the spear's lan–na–zha is the root method and why the spear is called the king of weapons.
ek: Lan and na deflect by a circle at the head, zha thrusts along the line; long reach plus control of the line dominates.

los.do: Assign the code and value for a described weapon accident.
ek: 73 weapon touches floor, loses grip, strikes body or deforms — 0.1 · 74 breaks — 0.2 · 75 dropped — 0.3 · 76 tassel/ribbon entangles or ornament falls — 0.1 · 66 throw-catch not caught correctly.

los.do: Explain how weapon mass and length change the timing of a body technique and the safe distance for a partner.
ek: A longer, heavier weapon has more rotational inertia: it starts late and stops late, so the body leads and the weapon follows; partner distance is measured to the tip, not the hand.

units.title: Jumps, balances and difficulty elements (nandu 难度)

los.do: Read a difficulty code and say its family and grade (e.g. 323A, 143B, 447A).
ek: First digit: 1 balance · 2 leg technique · 3 jump · 4 tumbling/ground. Letter: A 0.2 · B 0.3 · C 0.4.

los.do: Identify a jump from its description and give its name (pinyin, English) and changquan code.
ek: Tengkong feijiao 腾空飞脚 jumping slap 312A · xuanfengjiao 旋风脚 tornado 360 323A / 540 323B / 720 323C · tengkong bailian 腾空摆莲 lotus 360 324A / 540 324B / 720 324C · xuanzi 旋子 butterfly 333A · xuanzi zhuanti 旋子转体 butterfly twist 360 353B / 720 353C · cekongfan 侧空翻 aerial cartwheel 335A, with 360 twist 355B.

los.do: Identify a balance or sweep difficulty from its description and give its code and value.
ek: 111A grasp-foot balance (leg vertical) · 112A side-kick catch · 112C back-kick hold · 123A backward balance · 133B arms-spread balance · 153A ocean-exploring · 163A gazing-at-moon · 244A front sweep 540 · 244B 900.

los.do: Give the value of the same code in different events and explain why it differs.
ek: Taiji grades rotation lower: taiji 323A = tornado 180, 323B = 360, 323C = 540, while changquan 323A = 360. Each event's table is its own scale.

los.do: Identify the nanquan and taiji-specific difficulty elements from their descriptions.
ek: Nanquan: 346A stationary back flip, 346B single-step back flip, 415A jumping double side kick, 423A jumping cross-legged 360 to side fall, 447A carp kip-up (liyu dating 鲤鱼打挺). Taiji: 142A low-step sole-kick balance, 143A low balance leg forward, 143B leg inserted behind, 212A parting/heel kick.

iwuf-2019t: C p8–15 connection tables, landing suffixes 0–11

los.do: Name the landing position from a connection suffix and vice versa.
ek: 0 pubu · 1 mabu · 2 diebu · 3 tixi duli 提膝独立 single-leg knee-raise · 4 front split · 5 hurdler's split · 6 zuopan · 7 gongbu · 8 land on take-off foot · 9 weapon throw-catch · 10 scissor · 11 scorpion.

los.do: Choose the correct connection value for a described jump + landing in changquan (auto-checkable).
Choose the correct connection value for a described taiji or nanquan connection.
Explain the pattern in connection values: why more rotation and a single-leg landing score higher.
ek: More rotation leaves more residual spin to kill; a one-foot base (3) or a split (4) leaves less margin than mabu (1). The value prices the risk of a code-70/71/72 error.

los.do: Compute a C score from a declared list of elements and connections, applying the caps.
ek: Technique total ≤ 1.4, connection total ≤ 0.6; over the cap only the last registered element is reduced. 2 of 3 C-judges must confirm each element.

los.do: Design a difficulty plan that reaches the caps with the lowest-risk element set for a given ability profile.
ek: Five B jumps already give 1.5 (> 1.4); trade one C for two A when the C fails often — expected value = value × success rate − expected deductions.

los.do: State how a 10-point score splits for events with and without difficulty and which judge group awards each part.
ek: With difficulty: A quality of movement 5 · B overall performance 3 · C difficulty 2 (1.4 + 0.6). Without difficulty (2024): A 7, B 3.

los.do: Apply the panel rules to a set of raw judge marks and compute the A and B scores.
ek: A: 3 judges, a deduction stands only if ≥ 2 confirm it. B: 5 judges, drop high and low, average the middle 3, truncate (not round) to three decimals.

los.do: Assign the code and value for a described balance-loss error.
ek: 70 sway, shuffle or skip — 0.1 · 71 extra support (hand, elbow, knee touches) — 0.2 · 72 fall (shoulder, buttocks, trunk down) — 0.3 · 77 balance held < 2 s — 0.1 · 78 any part outside the carpet — 0.1 · 79 forgotten movement — 0.1.

los.do: Assign the code for a described jump or balance execution fault in changquan.
ek: 10–16 balances (bent legs, torso > 45°, leg below level) · 30 slapped toes below shoulder or slap missed · 31 hanging leg bent · 32 cartwheel legs bent ≥ 45° · 33 butterfly torso out of range or legs bent · 34 jumping snap leg below level.

los.do: Score a described full sequence: list every A deduction with its code and total them.
ek: Each code is per occurrence; a jump that lands short of the slap and then shuffles earns 30 and 70 separately.

los.do: Place a described performance into a B band and grade, justifying it with the criteria.
ek: Criteria: power, coordination, rhythm, style, choreography, music. Bands (difficulty events): superior 2.51–3.00 · average 1.91–2.50 · inferior 1.01–1.90, each split into three grades.

los.do: Assign the choreography code and value for a described structural or content fault.
ek: 80 missing/extra/altered technique — 0.1 or 0.2 · 81 missing/extra step — 0.1 · 82 missing nanquan vocalisation — 0.2 · 83 static pause > 3 s — 0.1 · 84 facing averted > 45° (changquan) or > 90° (taiji) — 0.1 · 85 no music or music with lyrics — 0.5.

los.do: Compute the head judge's time deduction for a routine of given length and event.
ek: Changquan, nanquan, weapons: adult optional 1:20–1:35; 0.1 per started 2 s outside. Taiji, group: 0.1 per started 5 s outside.

los.do: Compare the 2005 and 2019 rule tables for a code and explain why a drill must name its edition.
ek: 2003 revision introduced nandu (2 of 10 points), first used at the 2005 Worlds; codes were renumbered and criteria tightened by 2019; 2024 widened 'other errors' to 0.05–0.3.

los.do: Define jingshen, yanshen, jiezou and jin and identify which one a described performance lacks.
ek: Jingshen 精神 spirit/intent · yanshen 眼神 eyes leading the technique · jiezou 节奏 rhythm: fast–slow, hard–soft, rise–fall, motion–stillness · jin 劲 trained power, fajin 发劲 its release.

los.do: Mark the rhythm of a routine section (accelerations, stops, holds) and justify each against the style.
ek: A routine is phrased like music: build, burst, hold. Uniform tempo reads as flat even when technique is clean.

los.do: Explain 'hands, eyes, body, steps arrive together' (手眼身法步) and diagnose a described timing error.
ek: The eyes turn first, the stance and hand finish on the same beat; a hand that lands after the stance looks weak and reads as disconnected power.

los.do: Draft an optional routine plan that meets the time limit, mandatory techniques, direction and carpet-use rules.
ek: Use corners and centre, avoid > 45° averted facing and > 3 s static holds, place difficulty where fatigue is lowest.

los.do: Choose music and cut points for a routine and check the music rules.
ek: Instrumental only: lyrics or no music is code 85 (0.5) where music is required.

los.do: Define the core staged-combat safety terms and identify which one a described unsafe exchange violates.
ek: Distance: the measure that makes a technique safe · cue–reaction–action: the attacker cues, the partner reacts, then the action completes · eye contact confirms readiness · non-contact strikes stay out of distance.

los.do: Choose the camera angle that sells a described non-contact strike and explain why it works.
ek: Along the lens axis, depth vanishes: a strike that misses by 15 cm sideways to camera hides behind the target's head when shot over the shoulder.

los.do: Explain how a knap and a reaction sell an impact and pick the knap type for a described shot.
ek: Sound plus a reaction timed to the strike sells contact; body knap (self), clap knap, shared knap (both partners) — choose the one hidden from camera.

los.do: Adapt a taolu combination into a two-person screen phrase, keeping every strike off-line and every reaction cued.
ek: Taolu is shadow-fighting; screen work adds a partner, so each technique needs a target off-line, a cue and a repeatable mark for multiple takes.

los.do: Compare duilian (choreographed sparring) judging with screen-fight priorities.
ek: Duilian rewards realism, timing and clean contact control under the same A/B structure; the camera rewards readable shapes and reactions — both depend on partner trust and fixed distance.

los.do: Calculate flight time and jump height from takeoff vertical velocity (and the reverse) for a described jump.
ek: t_flight = 2v/g, h = v²/2g; 0.5 s of air needs v ≈ 2.45 m/s and h ≈ 0.31 m of CoM rise.

los.do: Explain which takeoff changes raise flight time, and identify the change that fixes a described 'no height' fault.
ek: Vertical impulse ∫(F − mg)dt: a short, stiff ground contact with full hip–knee–ankle extension and an upward arm drive. bio-xfj: takeoff knee ≈ 60°, short foot-pat contact gives larger vertical acceleration.

los.do: Explain where the angular momentum for a tornado kick or butterfly twist comes from and why it can't be added in the air.
ek: Friction torque from the feet on the floor (plus the arm and leg wind-up) generates L before takeoff; in flight no external torque acts about the CoM, so L is constant.

los.do: Predict how a shape change in flight alters spin rate and identify which change fixes a described under-rotation.
ek: L = Iω constant: pulling arms and legs toward the spin axis cuts I and raises ω. Rotations = ω·t/2π, so under-rotation is fixed by more L at takeoff, a tighter shape, or more flight time.

los.do: Explain why residual spin at landing causes shuffles and which landing shapes make it harder to kill.
ek: On touchdown the floor must apply an opposite torque; a wide base (mabu) supplies it easily, one foot or a split supplies little, so excess spin becomes a code-70 shuffle or a fall.

los.do: Explain the timing rule for the slap in xuanfengjiao and lotus kick and identify the fault when the slap is late.
ek: bio-xfj: the inward kick circle should be completed before the CoM peaks; slapping on the way down leaves no time to land and drops the slap below shoulder (code 30).

los.do: Explain how a landing reduces peak force and identify the fix for a described 'stiff landing'.
ek: F_avg = Δp/Δt: sequential ankle–knee–hip flexion lengthens stopping time; landing stiff-legged spikes force on knees and spine.

los.do: Explain why a balance holds or fails in terms of centre of mass and base of support.
ek: Static balance needs the CoM projection inside the base; single-leg balances (≥ 2 s, code 77) leave a base the size of one foot, so the trunk and raised leg must counter each other.

los.do: Identify a knee-valgus or knee-over-toe misalignment in a described landing or stance and explain the injury risk.
ek: Knees caving inward on landing loads the ACL and MCL; the same alignment is judged in stances (mabu knees buckle in, code 51).

los.do: State where wushu injuries concentrate and plan a prehab routine that targets those sites.
ek: Elite wushu study: 6.85 injuries / 1000 h, lower limb 47.6 %, then head/face (contact work); flat feet and shoulder asymmetry common. Ankle, knee and adductor/hamstring work goes first.

los.do: Plan a weekly jump and landing volume with progressions and identify signs to back off.
ek: Landings are the dose: count them; progress rotation before landing difficulty; mats and lower-rotation drills carry the reps; pain on landing or loss of height signals fatigue.

los.do: Explain how fatigue changes takeoff and landing mechanics and why difficulty goes early in a routine or take.
ek: Fatigue shortens flight, slows wind-up and softens landing control — all three raise the chance of 70–72 errors and injury.

los.do: Assign the points for a described sanda exchange under amateur rules.
ek: Punch to head or body 1 · kick to body 2 · kick to leg 1 · complete throw 2 · opponent exits ring 2 to the other fighter (representative amateur values; IWUF and classes vary).

los.do: Identify whether a described technique or target is legal in amateur sanda.
ek: Illegal: elbows, knees (amateur), joint locks, strikes to back of head, neck, spine, groin; clinch allowed only briefly before a throw or break.

los.do: Explain how the four methods ti, da, shuai, na (踢打摔拿) appear in sanda and in Duanwei content.
ek: Kick, strike, throw, seize; sanda emphasises the first three; kick-catch throws (jie tui shuai 接腿摔) punish kicks left extended.

los.do: Contrast TKD sparring habits with sanda and name the habit that the throw rule exploits.
ek: High, chambered, retracted-late kicks and an upright bounce stance invite catches and throws; sanda kicks are faster to recover and the stance is lower.

los.do: Place the milestones of modern wushu in order and say what each changed.
ek: 1928 Central Guoshu Institute · 1958 state standardisation of forms and grading · 1986 Chinese National Research Institute of Wushu · 2003 rules add nandu, first used 2005 Worlds · 2014 Youth Olympics demo · 2026 Dakar Youth Olympics.

los.do: Explain how standardised taolu differ from traditional forms and why the difference exists.
ek: Standard routines fix technique and content so performances can be judged against shared criteria; traditional forms keep lineage-specific methods and applications.

los.do: Name a duan from its number or badge and give its tier.
ek: Primary 1–3: blue, silver, gold eagle (青鹰 银鹰 金鹰) · Middle 4–6: blue, silver, gold tiger · Advanced 7–9: blue, silver, gold dragon; three pre-duan levels below.

los.do: State what each Duanwei level examines and what is added at each step.
ek: Evaluation: ethics and etiquette, theory, technique, skill. Each level's form goes solo → partner → applications; content builds 1 punching · 2 kicks · 3 grasping · 4 positioning · 5 wrestling · 6 all combined; high duan adds theory and contribution.

los.do: Map a goal (teaching, theory, a specific style) to the Duanwei textbook series and the duan that would test it.
ek: 4 theory books (ethics and etiquette, history, introduction, exam Q&A), 20 style books (changquan, Shaolin, taiji styles, xingyi, bagua, bajiquan…), 3 weapon courses (jianshu, duangun, erjiegun). Middle duan assumes ability to teach.

los.do: Perform the baoquan li salute correctly and explain its meaning in wude (martial ethics).
ek: Right fist covered by left palm at chest height; part of the etiquette Duanwei examines.
